headline:
MDCCCLXIII-MDCCCLXXII: TEN BREAKTHROUGHS on the TETRAHEDRON at the
center of Csaszar/Szilassi toroidal polyhedra.

DEEPEST GEOMETRIC INSIGHT: CSASZAR / C_2 = TETRAHEDRON.

Bokowski-Eggert (1986) proved every Csaszar realization has C_2
symmetry pairing 3 vertices with 3 vertices, fixing 1.  Under C_2
quotient: 4 = mu quotient vertices form a TETRAHEDRON.

Vertex count: 7 = Phi_6 = r*q + 1 (master substrate identity)
  1 fixed vertex (time axis) + 3 pairs of spatial vertices

TETRAHEDRON IS THE 3+1 SPACETIME PRIMITIVE:
  V=4=mu=q+1, E=6=g_2, F=4=mu, |Aut|=24=m_r (moonshine)
  1 time vertex + 3 = q space vertices

CSASZAR IS THE r-DOUBLE COVER OF SPACETIME:
  Edge/face expansion ratio = Phi_6 / r = 7/2 (substrate clean)
  Torus hole = topological defect from r-doubling
  K_7 cannot be planar -> wraps into torus

SZILASSI = face-dual r-doubled tetrahedron (V = dim(G_2) = 14)

Cross-dual identity: V(Csaszar) + V(Szilassi) = E_shared = g_1
                   = 7 + 14 = 21 = q * Phi_6

7 origami axioms = 7 Csaszar vertices = substrate folding rules
Time-axis vertex (fixed under C_2) = substrate ground state

The tetrahedron at the center is LITERALLY there:
Csaszar = r-doubled spacetime tetrahedron with closed timelike curve.
